newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index marginally up on local demand.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index marginally up on local demand.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20 share index gained marginally on improved local demand on Friday, bourse officials said.
The index rose 17.62 points to close at 3466.84. Turnover was posted at 18.5 million shillings traded on 635,948 shares compared to 12.1 million shillings on 366,061 on Thursday.
"Local investors are coming in now, it looks like a good time to buy," a broker said.
Bamburi Cement was traded at 41.25 from 40.25, Kenya National Mills at 44 from 38.50 and Kenya Commercial Bank at 102 unchanged.

For two weeks the market has been low as foreign investors have stayed away amid growing political tension. The tension was based on calls by an opposition-backed alliance for "minimum" constitutional reforms before general elections this year.
Kenya's ruling KANU party said on Thursday it had recommended that restrictive laws condemned in these "minimum reforms" go to parliament to be repealed or amended "if deemed necessary".
A bourse official said that although Friday had seen continuous trading the mood was still cautious, adding that most of the activity was on the normal boards.
A broker said the market was getting back to normal after political tensions plunged the bourse to a year low last week.
"The cooling down of political tensions is helping a lot," he said. "If it continues like this the (general) elections will be conducted very peacefully by African standards."

He said that as Kenyan investors perceived the market to be improving they were starting to trade ahead of large, foreign investors. "Local investors are grabbing shares before the big guys move into the market."
Local insurance companies are also starting to move cautiously into the market, after they were granted capital gains tax relief in this year's budget, a broker said.
Sasini Tea & Coffee edged up to close at 81.50 from 80.50 while Kakuzi was unchanged at 107.
Kenya Airways ended the week at 8.0 from 7.40, and Nation Printers & Publishers shed 11 to 101. Uchumi Supermarket eased to 37 from 37.50.
Barclays Bank was unchanged at 110 while Standard Chartered Bank eased to 50 shillings from 50.50.
Kenya Power & Lighting closed at 174 from 175 while Kenya Breweries closed at 57 unchanged.

The third issue of Central Bank of Kenya floating rate treasury bond traded 450,000 shillings at 101.5405 percent from 101.5309 percent while the fourth issue traded 11.45 million shillings at 101.6460 percent from 101.3430 percent.
